title: Finite products of stage sections on a colimit site
statement: In the filtered-colimit-site setting of lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites, let G(j) be abelian stage sheaves, theta the adjoint section transitions, H a diagram of their inverse images, E its specified identifications, and beta the units followed by E inverse; assume beta compatibility with H. Let c be a colimiting cocone of H. Fix i, any finite type A and objects X(t) of F(i). Suppose D:Under(i) -> Ab has specified isomorphisms eD(a) to the product over t:A of G(a.right)(F(a.hom)(X(t))). Suppose K is a cocone of D with eK identifying its point with the product over t:A of c.pt(V(i)(X(t))). Assume the transition maps of D, under eD, project to theta on every X(t), and the coprojections of K, under eD and eK, project to beta followed by c coprojections. Then Nonempty (IsColimit K). No complexes, chosen fibre products, or covering family enter this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09YP displayed Cech comparison, expanded with Sites Tags 09YM and 09YN (official tag pages consulted 2026-10-13)

proof.text: For each X(t), apply 09YM to the stage inverse images, insert the formulas into the colimit of H, and reindex the iterated filtered colimit along the final diagonal refinement. hobjects and harrows lift finite data and equations to a common refinement. The adjunction-unit identifications and the assumed beta compatibility give the exact theta transitions and beta/c coprojections.

Every Q-cover is the image of a finite stage cover by hQ and hfinite. Filtered sheaf colimits on Q are therefore computed on sections, by the finite-covering sheaf equalizer argument. Apply the abelian fixed-site section comparison to identify the outer colimit with c.pt sections.

Commute the filtered colimit with the finite product over A, and apply the scalar section comparisons. The supplied projection equations identify D and K with this finite product diagram and its canonical cocone, since product projections determine all maps. Transfer its colimit universal property across eD and eK. For empty A both sides are zero; for singleton A this is the scalar formula.

theorem colimitSite_finiteProduct_sections_isColimit
    {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u}) (P : ∀ j, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ j, (P j).HasIsos] [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderComposition]
    [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderBaseChange] [∀ j, (P j).HasPullbacks]
    (hfinite : ∀ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
      Finite R.uncurry)
    (hcover : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → R.map (F.map a).toFunctor ∈ P k ((F.map a).toFunctor.obj X))
    (hpullback : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
        PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (F.map a).toFunctor)
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k), PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafPullback (F.map a).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck)]
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k), PreservesFiniteColimits
      (sheafPullback (F.map a).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck)]
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [Q.HasIsos] [Q.IsStableUnderComposition] [Q.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [Q.HasPullbacks]
    (hQ : ∀ (Y : V.pt) (R : Presieve Y), R ∈ Q Y ↔
      ∃ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (S : Presieve X) (h : (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X = Y),
        S ∈ P j X ∧ h ▸ S.map (V.ι.app j).toFunctor = R)
    [∀ j, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck]
    (G : ∀ j, Sheaf (P j).toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (θ : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (G j).obj ⟶ (F.map a).toFunctor.op ⋙ (G k).obj)
    (H : J ⥤ Sheaf Q.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (E : ∀ j, H.obj j ≅
      (sheafPullback (V.ι.app j).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u}
        (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj (G j)) :
    let β := fun (j : J) (X : F.obj j) ↦
      (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (V.ι.app j).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u}
        (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).unit.app (G j)).hom.app (op X)) ≫
        (E j).inv.hom.app (op ((V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X))
    (∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X : F.obj j),
      Arrow.mk (β j X ≫ (H.map a).hom.app (op ((V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X))) =
        Arrow.mk ((θ j k a).app (op X) ≫ β k ((F.map a).toFunctor.obj X))) →
    ∀ (c : Cocone H), IsColimit c →
    ∀ (i : J) {A : Type u} [Finite A] (X : A → F.obj i)
      (D : Under i ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (eD : ∀ a : Under i, D.obj a ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of
        (∀ t : A, (G a.right).obj.obj (op ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t)))))
      (K : Cocone D)
      (eK : K.pt ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of
        (∀ t : A, c.pt.obj.obj (op ((V.ι.app i).toFunctor.obj (X t))))),
      (∀ (a a' : Under i) (b : a ⟶ a') (t : A),
        Arrow.mk ((eD a).inv ≫ D.map b ≫ (eD a').hom ≫
          AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (Pi.evalAddMonoidHom _ t)) =
        Arrow.mk (AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (Pi.evalAddMonoidHom
          (fun t ↦ (G a.right).obj.obj
            (op ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t)))) t) ≫
          (θ a.right a'.right b.right).app
            (op ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t))))) →
      (∀ (a : Under i) (t : A),
        Arrow.mk ((eD a).inv ≫ K.ι.app a ≫ eK.hom ≫
          AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (Pi.evalAddMonoidHom _ t)) =
        Arrow.mk (AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (Pi.evalAddMonoidHom
          (fun t ↦ (G a.right).obj.obj
            (op ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t)))) t) ≫
          β a.right ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t)) ≫
          (c.ι.app a.right).hom.app
            (op ((V.ι.app a.right).toFunctor.obj
              ((F.map a.hom).toFunctor.obj (X t)))))) →
      Nonempty (IsColimit K)
